name: Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 4

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the GRHPR gene
Elevated urinary oxalate excretion above age-adjusted reference ranges
Recurrent nephrolithiasis or nephrocalcinosis documented by imaging
Progressive renal impairment or end-stage renal disease in absence of other causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic variants in GRHPR gene plus elevated urinary oxalate excretion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis due to overlap with other hyperoxalurias.

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain secondary to renal osteodystrophy

laboratory: Elevated plasma oxalate levels especially in renal failure
Normal or mildly elevated glycolate levels
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephrocalcinosis and kidney stones
Echocardiogram in systemic oxalosis cases showing cardiac deposits
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in GRHPR gene confirming diagnosis
other: Kidney biopsy may show calcium oxalate crystal deposition
Histopathology of bone may reveal oxalate deposits in advanced disease

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset and more severe renal failure
Mutations in GRHPR gene but different biochemical profile
Less severe clinical course compared to PH1
Associated with enteric diseases or dietary oxalate overload
No pathogenic variants in PH genes

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure in a young patient
Recurrent calcium oxalate kidney stones refractory to standard treatment
Family history of early-onset nephrolithiasis or renal failure
references: Hoppe B, et al. Primary hyperoxaluria type 4: clinical and genetic characterization. Kidney Int. 2020.
Liebow A, et al. The expanding spectrum of primary hyperoxaluria: diagnosis and management. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2022.
